extracted.intended_audience: recipients of EPA financial assistance (states, grantees, local governments, universities), EPA staff, civil rights practitioners, and community/stakeholder audiences interested in Title VI and environmental justice
extracted.subtask_short: Title VI compliance and environmental justice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and Executive Order 12898 interact with environmental justice, including who is covered, prohibited discriminatory practices, procedural complaint mechanisms, and EPA responsibilities for enforcement and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title VI nondiscrimination prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Title VI prohibits recipients of federal financial assistance (e.g., states, universities, local governments) from discriminating on the basis of race, color, or national origin in their programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory requirement (Civil Rights Act of 1964) that applies to entities that receive federal financial assistance. EPA has had Title VI regulations since 1973 to implement this mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: Title VI applies to recipients of federal financial assistance (not EPA itself)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title VI is a federal law that applies to federal financial assistance recipients (i.e., persons or entities that receive EPA financial assistance) and not to EPA itself as the Executive Order does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand applicability before bringing or assessing claims — the recipient status of an entity determines whether Title VI's prohibitions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12898 directive on environmental justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 12898 directs federal agencies to identify and address, as appropriate, disproportionally high adverse human health and environmental effects of their programs, policies, and activities on minority populations and low-income populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Order instructs agencies (including EPA) to incorporate achieving environmental justice into their missions; it is broader in focus than Title VI and focuses on identifying and addressing disparate environmental/health impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential Memorandum requirement for non-discriminatory criteria/methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Title VI, each Federal agency shall ensure that all programs or activities receiving Federal financial assistance that affect human health or the environment do not directly, or through contractual or other arrangements, use criteria, methods, or practices that discriminate on the basis of race, color, or national origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit direction accompanying Executive Order 12898 emphasizing that agencies must ensure their funding recipients avoid discriminatory criteria, methods, or practices — including indirect discrimination via contracts or other arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint mechanism under Title VI
rubrics_metrics.description: Title VI allows persons to file administrative complaints with the federal departments and agencies that provide financial assistance alleging discrimination based on race, color, or national origin by recipients of federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals or groups believing they were discriminated against by a recipient of federal financial assistance can file an administrative complaint with the funding agency (e.g., EPA).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA responsibility to ensure funds do not subsidize discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Title VI, EPA has a responsibility to ensure that its funds are not being used to subsidize discrimination based on race, color, or national origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA administers and enforces Title VI for programs it funds; EPA's Office of Civil Rights is responsible for the Agency's administration of Title VI, including investigation of complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection of Title VI and environmental justice in enforcement and programs
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title VI civil rights complaint may raise environmental justice issues when challenging a recipient's activity; EPA, in complying with Executive Order 12898, can also ensure the programs it funds consider disproportionately high adverse human health and environmental effects on minority and low-income populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating programs or enforcement actions (e.g., a state-run clean air program funded by EPA), consider both nondiscrimination obligations under Title VI and EJ considerations under the Executive Order; complaints may invoke both frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical example of applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state agency receives funds from EPA to run a clean air program, that state recipient is legally prohibited from discriminating on the basis of race, color or national origin under Title VI when engaging in clean air enforcement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete program examples to determine where Title VI applies and to identify potential discriminatory practices in program implementation or enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative responsibility and points of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's Office of Civil Rights is responsible for the Agency's administration of Title VI, including investigation of such complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should direct Title VI-related complaints, questions, or reports about EPA-funded programs to EPA's Office of Civil Rights or use the provided Contact Us resources on the EPA website.
